scope: Read-only review of six final authored Korean/English paragraphs, exact collected publishing strings, selected printed pp.110–113, and existing actual native/release-game evidence. No full-book reread, source fetch, platform action or media change.

paragraphConformance.sourceClaim: Payload goal explains why escorting and fighting beside the cart changes the spatial requirement. Present release-game recording introduces the phenomenon; historic problem is explicitly past tense.
paragraphConformance.review: Goal and changed action precede tunnel failure; core-mechanic framing is retained through the concrete mode rule.

paragraphConformance.sourceClaim: Early Badwater prototypes reused a standard tunnel width; playtesting exposed players blocked by the cart.
paragraphConformance.review: Historic problem and causal explanation retained; no historic measurements or prototype footage asserted.

paragraphConformance.sourceClaim: Both player and cart must fit the circulation space.
paragraphConformance.review: Added prerequisite beside the source example: centered cart, two side gaps, and our collision capsule in a synchronized overhead view. Symmetry applies to our experiment, not all maps.

paragraphConformance.sourceClaim: Tunnel widening after playtesting improved circulation for players and cart.
paragraphConformance.review: One-variable own-engine comparison inserts a visible mechanism before returning to the original actual design outcome.

paragraphConformance.sourceClaim: Game spaces should accommodate avatar and gameplay-element movement metrics.
paragraphConformance.review: Canonical Gameplay Metrics term follows the mechanism; body/door, jump reach and shared space are reference dimensions, not measurements from the release-game clip.

paragraphConformance.sourceClaim: Pushing metrics toward their limits can create deliberate tension; a narrow horror corridor can make one enemy threatening.
paragraphConformance.review: Necessary limit retained after metrics; conclusion returns to the cart-escort action rather than an always-widen rule.

mainClaim.text: Test the intended player action alongside the gameplay object; fitting the cart alone does not demonstrate usable player circulation. Widening is appropriate for this escort action, not a universal level-design rule.
mainClaim.order: Mode goal → historical blocked-tunnel problem → added collision/clearance explanation → widened result → gameplay metrics → purpose-dependent narrow-space contrast → cart-escort conclusion.

nativeClaimReview.fixedConditions: Same cart, character/collision capsule, initial world coordinates, commanded movement sequence, speed and cameras; wall spacing is the changed scene input.
nativeClaimReview.observableResult: Narrow trial blocks movement beside the cart; wide trial permits passage. Different final lateral positions are collision results, not changed starting coordinates.
limits: Only our experiment yields the shown collision outline and gap values; no TF2 internal collider or historic tunnel dimensions are claimed.
The two captured fixed-width trials are compared editorially; the film does not establish that moving walls are dynamically simulated.
General narrow-corridor tension illustration is explicitly a conceptual diagram, not implemented enemy AI or measured commercial horror gameplay.
